priority_justification: Over-temperature shutdown caused total loss of generator backup power. If this recurs during a real utility outage, the facility has no backup. Thermal degradation risks engine damage (warped head, blown gasket). Must be resolved before next outage test.

possible_causes: The following are possible causes, NOT confirmed diagnoses. The fault has NOT been attributed to mechanical failure: 1. SENSOR: ATS position sensor error — sensor may report UTILITY incorrectly while the switch actually transferred. 2. SENSOR: ATS position limit switch intermittent fault. 3. MEASUREMENT: Transfer-confirmation logic artefact — the DSE6120 confirmation input may have a transient or wiring issue. 4. CONTROL: ATS control circuit fault — relay, contactor coil, or actuator command not reaching the mechanism. 5. TOPOLOGY: Bypass path or dual-source configuration not modelled in this dataset — the facility may have a secondary transfer path. 6. SIMULATION: Data generation artefact — this is simulated data; the FAILED status may represent a modelling choice, not a real fault. NOTE: Generator output was healthy (V, Hz normal), so any fault is in the ATS transfer path or its sensing, not the generator.
missing_evidence: 1. Load-bus voltage — critical for confirming whether building had power during this period (NOT available in this dataset). 2. ATS position sensor raw signal — to verify if position reading is accurate or if sensor is faulty. 3. ATS contactor mechanical position — visual inspection needed. 4. ATS control circuit voltage and continuity. 5. Facility single-line diagram — to verify single-ATS topology assumption and rule out bypass paths. 6. ATS motor/actuator coil resistance. 7. Wiring continuity from DSE6120 to ATS. 8. ATS maintenance/inspection history (last serviced date). 9. ATS manufacturer model and specifications. 10. Environmental conditions (moisture, dust in ATS enclosure).
suggested_action: 1. Verify topology — obtain facility single-line diagram to confirm single-ATS assumption and check for bypass paths. 2. Inspect ATS position sensor and limit switches — do NOT assume mechanical failure before ruling out sensor issues. 3. Test ATS control circuit voltage and relay operation. 4. Measure ATS motor/actuator coil resistance; replace if out of spec. 5. Inspect wiring between DSE6120 and ATS for corrosion or damage. 6. Manually exercise ATS transfer to verify mechanical freedom. 7. Install or verify load-bus voltage monitoring to confirm building power status during transfer events. 8. Schedule ATS manufacturer service if internal fault suspected. 9. Review ATS maintenance history — last service was radiator/ATS contact inspection (see maintenance_history.csv).
priority_justification: Generator was fully functional but ATS transfer was not confirmed — the generator was not feeding the building load (current=0A). Whether the building had power from utility during this period cannot be confirmed without load-bus voltage data. However, the ATS transfer-confirmation failure itself is critical: if the utility was truly failed and the ATS could not transfer, the standby system's core function is compromised. ATS transfer reliability is the single most critical function of a standby system. Must be investigated and resolved before returning to service.
